title: The M0 dwarf Gaia DR3 2698173741829957888 has dimmed aperiodically since 2010 and needs grains near 1 um; five dwarf dimmers move like matched field stars, so their old ages reflect the search volume
abstract: Prior campaign studies found deep dust dimming of old field dwarfs (Gaia20cdd, Gaia DR3 2870538750879109504). A blind search found more dimmers, but nobody examined the deepest of them, Gaia DR3 2698173741829957888 (G2698). We used ZTF DR24, Pan-STARRS1, 2MASS, AllWISE, NEOWISE, CatWISE2020 and Gaia DR3. G2698 is an M0/K7 dwarf (T_eff 4100 K) at 0.95 kpc, 0.49 kpc below the plane, with no infrared excess and no XP H-alpha emission. In ZTF (2018-2025) it is more than 0.3 mag faint on 47 percent of nights and more than 1 mag faint on 20 percent (4 times Gaia20cdd); the deepest drop is 2.6 mag in r. PS1 and AllWISE show deep states in 2010-2013. On 303 nights a partial-cover model (13 percent of the light uncovered) fits better than a full screen (delta 2lnL = 31.6), with k_g = 1.31 and k_i = 0.85. Eleven NEOWISE visits give W1 and W2 depths of 0.28 (0.20-0.36) and 0.11 (0.03-0.20) times the r depth. Mie models need a_max = 0.97-3.6 um (astrosilicate) or 0.44-2.4 um (graphite) for n(a) ~ a^-3.5, or only grains below 0.025 um; interstellar grains are excluded. Thus the three deep dimmers have three different dust populations. The 1156-d periodogram peak is not significant against long-time-scale red noise (false-alarm probability 0.14-0.67) and does not predict the 2010-2017 data. For five dwarf dimmers, the sky velocities agree with 662-4,696 matched Gaia DR3 field stars each (Fisher p = 0.61), so the old ages follow from the high-latitude search volume. Limitations: no spectra or radial velocities, detections-only ZTF data, 11 NEOWISE visits, spherical grains, five stars in the kinematic test. display.caption: G2698 from 2000 to 2025: ZTF, Pan-STARRS1 and 2MASS (top), WISE W1 and W2 (bottom). Deep dimming occurs in every year with data since 2010.
(a) ZTF colour trajectory of G2698 with full-screen and partial-cover fits. (b) NEOWISE W1 and W2 depths against the simultaneous optical depth: kappa1 = 0.28.
Sky velocities of five dwarf dimmers (red) against matched Gaia DR3 field stars (grey). The dimmers are not faster than their neighbours (Fisher p = 0.61).
